author: emil
text: no, and honestly thats the bit i'd want spelled out more than the spelling. let me think through that for a sec... it only comes back `True` where we actually took bytes off the message. a run that raises with four lines of stderr goes in whole, nothing removed, so the flag stays down even though the run failed

author: emil
text: yup, its answering "is what youre reading all of it" and nothing else. we need to be intentional here because the obvious reading is the wrong one — anyone consuming it as "did this blow up" gets a false negative on every short failure

author: gideon
text: ya so basically that test isnt looking at the result object the way you think. it walks `CodeExecutionResult.model_fields` and then goes row by row and asserts each row only has keys out of that set

author: dario
text: sure but the rows come out of the same execution. if the model grows a field the rows should just grow it too no

author: gideon
text: no thats the bit. a row is stdout, stderr and files and thats it, theres never an exception on one. the executor raises before it ever gets as far as building a row, so `error_truncated` has nothing to hang off of

author: gideon
text: so its not going in there. the marker we put in the stderr text is already carrying that tbh

author: dario
text: huh. i had it filed in my head as a failed run coming back as a row with the traceback sitting in stderr

author: gideon
text: honestly though thats hte confusing part, the traceback *does* land in stderr when the users code fails. its only the executor itself dying that never produces a row at all
